Great Britain's women's rowing duo, Helen Glover and Heather Stanning, won their second consecutive Olympic gold medal in the women's eight event, finishing 1.2 seconds clear of New Zealand with a time of 7 minutes 18.29 seconds, while also becoming unbeaten in 39 races and defending their London 2012 title.

Strictly Come Dancing professionals Steve and Ola Jordan have spoken out about the "bullying" claims that surfaced earlier this month, saying they chose to show unity and focus on their dancing, rather than responding to the allegations.

The UK's inflation rate dropped to 2.6% in June, contrary to economists' expectations of no change, leading to a decline in the value of the pound, which initially lifted the FTSE 100 share index before it closed down slightly.

British actress Vicky McClure was mistakenly thrown off a tram in Nottingham in 2015 after a conductor, unaware of her free travel offer due to a ceremony naming a tram in her honor, asked her for a ticket, which was later resolved with an apology from Nottingham Express Transit.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross, found murdered in a London river in 2014, will investigate whether government and police failures contributed to her death and allowed the chief suspect, a Latvian builder with a murder conviction, to live unchecked in the UK, despite him having been convicted of murdering his wife in Latvia in 1998.

A study by The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling found that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate decreased from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest rate at 33% and Inverurie having the lowest at 1%.

Rory McWhirter, a man from Edinburgh, was sentenced to custody for a "fairly sophisticated" fraudulent scheme in which he used fake births and marriage certificates to claim £34,380 in benefits, including tax credits, child benefits, and a maternity grant, after being caught by staff at an Aberdeen registry office where he had previously registered false births.

Clashes between Shia residents and Saudi security forces in the Eastern Province city of Awamiya have intensified, resulting in at least seven deaths, with residents accusing the authorities of firing randomly at homes and cars and attempting to demolish the historic quarter.

Young people in Belfast, including those attending a job training course, express frustration with their job search experiences and feel that politicians should be more proactive and address the region's employment and healthcare issues, rather than being focused on personal agendas.

The chief executive of Barnet Council, Andrew Travers, left the authority by "mutual agreement" after an investigation was launched into the borough's polling station issues on election day, where voters were initially turned away due to missing names on the poll list, and he was temporarily succeeded by Deputy Chief Executive John Hooton.
Cardiff City manager Neil Warnock has given midfielder Peter Whittingham time to consider a new contract offer, stating that the offer remains on the table and will not be withdrawn.

A BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation has revealed evidence of suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, prompting a doubles representative to express concern and suggest additional funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit (TIU).

A 60-year-old man, believed to be a customer, surrendered to police after allegedly producing a firearm at a Barclays bank in Northfield, Birmingham, with no customers or staff harmed, and he was taken to hospital for an assessment.

Mohammed Ali, a 31-year-old computer software programmer, has denied a charge of attempting to possess a chemical weapon after allegedly ordering 500mg of ricin, a deadly toxin, online through a black market deal that was actually an undercover operation by the FBI, in which he unknowingly took delivery of harmless powder.

The chief executive of Rodney Parade Limited, which owns the stadium used by Newport County, responded to the club's manager by citing the high cost of maintaining the pitch due to the football club's frequent game postponements and abandonments, despite the Dragons also experiencing issues with the same pitch.

A survey by Aviva UK Health found that nearly two-thirds of workers reported going to work while unwell, with many fearing a heavy workload upon their return, highlighting a potential "false economy" for businesses due to presenteeism.

The UK's FTSE 100 index closed almost flat, with mixed performances from various companies, as the Bank of England kept interest rates at 0.25% and trimmed its 2017 growth forecast, with some analysts expecting a rate rise that didn't materialize.

Roman Seleznev, the son of a Russian MP, has been found guilty of 38 out of 40 charges related to a hacking scheme that stole and sold almost 3 million credit card numbers from US businesses, including pizza chains in Washington state, between 2008 and 2014.
US President Donald Trump denied having any recordings of his conversations with former FBI Director James Comey, confirming Comey's hope that there were indeed tapes.

Liberty, a global steel and commodities business led by Sanjeev Gupta, is expected to submit a bid to acquire Tata's remaining UK steel assets, with the support of the UK government and potential financial backing from the Australian bank Macquarie, following a formal process of submitting a letter of intent.

East Midlands councils have proposed a tram line connecting the region, including Nottingham and Derby, to East Midlands Airport and the proposed HS2 station at Toton, with estimated costs ranging from £180m to £200m.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world champion, won the Masters tournament with a 10-1 victory over Barry Hawkins, attributing his success to modifying his game to remain competitive against younger players by adding more power and adapting his strategy.

Severe storms in Poland over the weekend killed six people, including two Girl Guides, and damaged thousands of homes, causing an estimated eight million cubic meters of lumber to be brought down across 45,000 hectares of forest.

Spanish singer Enrique Iglesias suffered a severe injury to his hand while attempting to retrieve a drone camera at a concert in Tijuana, Mexico, and will require several weeks to recover from reconstructive surgery, including correcting a fracture in addition to the initial damage.

The Leeds Rhinos secured a 54-0 victory over the Warrington Wolves in Super League, with Matt Parcell scoring a hat-trick and the hosts keeping the Wire scoreless despite a disjointed performance from the visitors.

William "Plum" Smith, a key figure in the 1994 loyalist ceasefire, has passed away, with tributes from the Deputy First Minister Martin McGuinness and former PUP leader Brian Ervine praising his commitment to peace and his efforts to bring loyalist paramilitaries into the peace process, including his work as chairman of the PUP and part of the party's negotiating team around the Good Friday Agreement.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old Royal British Legion poppy collector from Bristol, has been selling poppies for over 75 years, including the past 12 years at the entrance to Bristol Cathedral, in memory of her late husband and others who died in both world wars.
Shimon Peres, a former Israeli president and prime minister who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994 for his role in negotiating peace accords with the Palestinians, has died at the age of 92.

A survey of Queen's University staff in Northern Ireland found that while two-thirds of staff were proud to work there and 89% found their work interesting, concerns were raised about leadership and change management, with only 29% agreeing that senior leaders provided effective leadership and fewer than a third gave positive responses to questions about leadership and direction.

The US Navy's X-47B unmanned jet, designed by Northrop Grumman, successfully completed its maiden flight, reaching an altitude of 5,000 feet and demonstrating its advanced radar-evading capabilities and tailless design, marking a significant step towards the development of a new generation of unmanned drones.

Airbus has reduced its production target for the A380 double-decker jet to 12 in 2018 and eight in 2019, citing low short-term sales prospects, while also facing production delays and reliability issues with its A320neo engine supplier Pratt & Whitney, in addition to operating the A380 at a marginal loss.

Scientists have observed a devastating 40% coral death at the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea, highlighting the need for drastic action to reduce global warming, as even a 2-degree temperature cap may not be enough to save coral reefs in shallow water ecosystems, particularly when combined with local weather fluctuations.

Scientists have discovered a protein, Hi1a, in the venom of Australian funnel web spiders that shows "great promise as a future stroke treatment" by blocking acid-sensing ion channels in the brain, which are key drivers of brain damage after a stroke, and may provide some protection to the core brain region most affected by oxygen deprivation.

Oldham Athletic took the lead in the fifth minute with a Peter Clarke header, but Bradford City equalized in the 57th minute after a penalty was awarded when Josh Cullen was fouled by Ousmane Fane, with Billy Clarke scoring the equalizer from the spot.

A study published in Nature has shown that the experimental Alzheimer's drug aducanumab is safe and may slow memory decline, but experts are cautious due to the early stages of development and the need for larger, more definitive trials to confirm its effects, particularly given the high dropout rate of 40 patients, mostly due to side effects.
Oldham Roughyeds, a part-time team in the second tier, secured a 28-24 surprise victory over Super League side Hull KR.

BBC director general Tony Hall outlined plans for the corporation's next decade, including becoming an "open BBC" with partnerships and collaborations, but also acknowledged that funding cuts would lead to the loss or reduction of some services, with potential areas of cut including streaming news replacing rolling news, BBC Four, and the need for "some existing services" to no longer be needed in future.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has expressed concern about a rise in hate attacks in the UK since the EU referendum, calling for politicians to promote "accurate information and respectful debate" to address the growing divisions and tensions in society.

Nigel Farage's former deputy, Suzanne Evans, has announced she would have liked to run for UKIP leadership but was blocked by a "handful of people at the top" due to her six-month ban for publicly criticising a fellow candidate and holding herself out as a party spokeswoman without authority, and is now endorsing councillor Lisa Duffy as the best chance for the party to "change, to grow and to thrive".

A new grading system will be introduced in England, replacing letters with numbers, and coursework will be scrapped for most subjects, with the changes starting with pupils due to take GCSE exams in 2018.
Retired US General David Petraeus expressed his willingness to serve under President-elect Donald Trump if asked, stating that as a military officer, "the only response can be: 'yes, Mr President'."

US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has met with newly elected Egyptian President Mohammed Mursi, praising Egypt's democratic transition and urging compromise to avoid confrontation between Mursi's supporters and the country's military leaders, with Clinton also praising the military council for its interim leadership.

Derek Bruder, a witness to the 1989 Hillsborough disaster, testified that he was visited by a police inspector who allegedly pressured him to change his statement about the vital signs of a 15-year-old boy, Kevin Williams, whom he had tried to resuscitate, claiming the inspector's actions were a deliberate attempt to alter the evidence, but the inspector denied any wrongdoing.
Oh Wonder's second album, Ultralife, explores the theme of human connection and resilience, inspired by the duo's own experiences and the stories of their fans who have been impacted by their music.
Bertrand Traore scored the opening goal for Chelsea, but Mame Biram Diouf equalized with a header from Xherdan Shaqiri's cross in a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge.

Three scientists, William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu, have made groundbreaking discoveries that have led to the development of life-saving drugs to treat diseases affecting over 3.4 billion people worldwide, including malaria, river blindness, and elephantiasis, with Campbell and Omura developing ivermectin and Tu discovering artemisinin.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation has called for accountability and the removal of South African President Jacob Zuma, citing his alleged corruption and the misuse of state resources, as the country's democracy faces a "real threat" under his rule, specifically referencing the alleged undue influence of the Gupta family.

Miranda Hart made her West End debut in the musical "Annie" at London's Piccadilly Theatre, receiving largely positive reviews for her performance as the villainous orphanage owner Miss Hannigan, in a role that took her "outside her comfort-zone".

Newcastle United secured a 2-0 win over West Ham United, their first in six league games, with Jonjo Shelvey playing a key role in both goals, as they moved out of the relegation zone at the expense of Swansea City.

UK supermarkets including Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's have cut the price of diesel by up to 2p per litre, with diesel now cheaper than petrol for the first time since July 2001, due to lower wholesale diesel costs and increased supply of diesel from refineries outside the UK.

The 70th UN General Assembly, attended by African leaders, serves as a crucial platform for addressing the continent's pressing issues, including poverty, hunger, and conflict, while also underscoring the UN's vital role in providing peacekeeping forces and support to Africa's development and self-determination, amidst ongoing challenges such as food crises, Ebola outbreaks, and accusations of misconduct by UN forces.

Suffolk police are searching for ecstasy pills containing the highly toxic class-A drug PMMA, a potent hallucinogenic stimulant, which has been linked to at least 22 deaths in the past year and may still be in circulation, potentially disguised with different logos.

UKIP donor Arron Banks has criticized the party's current leadership, calling for a return to a "blue UKIP" strategy of copying Conservative policies, not "red UKIP" strategy of copying Labour policies on the NHS, and the re-engagement of former leader Nigel Farage.

The article explores the rise of "Invisible Girlfriend" and "Invisible Boyfriend," a service that allows users to create a fake online partner for companionship, with thousands of users paying for the service, and the company's CEO citing reasons such as getting parents off their back or practicing flirting as motivations, with the service being used by both men and women.

Germany's dominant 2-0 victory over Poland showcased their attacking prowess, with standout performances from Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, and Mario Gotze, but also highlighted potential defensive vulnerabilities that Scotland may be able to exploit in their upcoming match, particularly with their full-backs caught high up the pitch.

Bristol City's Tammy Abraham scored his 22nd goal of the season, but the team could only draw 1-1 with Blackburn Rovers, remaining four points above the relegation zone with three games to play in the Championship.

Scotland's players aim to send departing coach Vern Cotter out on a high by beating Ireland on Saturday, despite facing a tough task against a strong Irish side that has won 14 of 17 Six Nations matches between the two teams, with Ireland's Joe Schmidt having pinpointed Scotland's weaknesses and Rory Best expecting a punishing set-piece battle.

Celtic secured a 2-0 victory over Kilmarnock, with Stefan Scepovic scoring twice, including a goal after the break, as the visitors' chances were dented by the dismissal of their key defender, Pascali, in the first half, and John Guidetti scoring on a free-kick shortly after Pascali's red card.

According to an international study by the OECD, Northern Irish pupils reported higher levels of life satisfaction than their counterparts in the UK, with an average satisfaction score of 7.24 out of 10, but still struggled with anxiety, bullying, and excessive internet use.

Crystal Palace came from behind to defeat Everton 3-2, with goals from Mile Jedinak, Fraizer Campbell, and Yannick Bolasie securing the win after Everton had taken an early lead through Romelu Lukaku and later equalized through Leighton Baines' penalty.

Gary Carter, a 36-year-old freelance sports journalist, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green, London, after an altercation, and has been hospitalized for surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain.
Tinie Tempah discusses his new album Youth, which marks his return to his roots and reconnects him with his friends, after feeling disconnected from reality due to his busy career.

Mobile operators, including O2 and Vodafone, are set to discuss with the government and communications regulator Ofcom the possibility of accelerating the allocation of spectrum to launch 4G networks in the UK by May or June, potentially allowing EE to announce its 4G launch date sooner, but also benefiting O2, which is hopeful of launching 4G services in summer 2013.

The UK Conservative government has scrapped the policy of providing free school lunches to all children in the first three years of primary school, citing concerns over its cost-effectiveness, despite some schools having invested heavily in catering facilities and achieving significant benefits from the program, including increased meal uptake and improved student health.

Israeli security forces are conducting a massive manhunt for a gunman who opened fire on a crowded street in Tel Aviv, wounding four people, with the motive unclear and possibilities including a terrorist attack, hate crime, or link to organised crime.

Scottish musician Dean Owens' song "Dora" sparked a search that led to the discovery of his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona's grave in Tomnahurich Cemetery, Inverness, after a local resident and family historian helped uncover details about Salvona's colorful life as a circus owner and lion tamer.

At the 2024 Glastonbury festival, organizers have introduced sustainable, recycled stainless steel pint cups, made from 80% recycled steel, as part of their efforts to promote a "reusable revolution" and support the UK steel industry.

Rescue efforts in Nepal continue as a 15-year-old boy and a woman in her 20s are pulled from collapsed buildings, while others are still trapped, and concerns grow over the pace of relief efforts, health risks, and contaminated water affecting survivors.

JP Morgan's senior executive, Daniel Pinto, stated that the bank may relocate between 500 and 1,000 jobs to Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg as part of contingency plans for Brexit, with other major banks also announcing plans to move jobs out of London.

Police in Ferguson, Missouri, broke up a crowd of about 150 protesters with a curfew in place after a person was shot and critically wounded in an unrelated incident, while the city continues to grapple with the aftermath of the fatal shooting of 18-year-old Michael Brown by a white police officer nine days earlier.

Shadow home secretary Diane Abbott has criticized Prime Minister Theresa May for allowing police officer numbers to fall during her tenure as Home Secretary, a claim the Conservatives have dismissed as "dangerous" and "desperate", but Abbott argues that the cuts have compromised public safety.

Wales suffered their heaviest loss in nine years, being routed 46-6 by the world champion New Zealand All Blacks in the final Test, conceding 16 tries in the three matches and losing their 29th consecutive match against the team, with the losses including a 39-21 first Test defeat and a 36-22 second Test defeat.

Five people, including a father-son duo, a retired navy engineer, a photographer, and a British ex-pat, died after a whale-watching boat capsized off the coast of British Columbia, Canada, with officials crediting the quick response of local residents for saving 21 of the 27 people on board, including the photographer's mother who was rescued.

Myanmar's government and several of its rebel groups signed a collective agreement, seen as a step towards a lasting political settlement, but the deal does not halt any conflicts and several major groups, including the largest, the United Wa State Army, did not sign the agreement.

A Northern Irish man with 15 convictions for sexual offences obtained a court order to remove a Facebook page that posted his photograph and threatening comments, citing harassment and human rights concerns, after a judge ruled the page's contents risked infringing the man's human rights.
Apple's email to publishers inviting them to join its upcoming news app presumes acceptance of its terms, including indemnifying Apple and allowing ad placement, unless publishers explicitly opt out.

Residents of the US territory of Guam are expressing concern and anxiety over North Korea's threats, with some stockpiling food and others feeling caught in the crossfire between President Trump and Kim Jong-un, despite the governor's reassurance that the island is prepared and there is currently no immediate threat.

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Sentinel-1b satellite, launched by a Soyuz rocket from French Guiana, will work alongside its predecessor to map the entire Earth every six days, providing data on pollution, icebergs, and land subsidence, among other applications, as part of the Copernicus Earth observation programme.

The pound's 1% gain and the stock market's 2% drop are being interpreted by market watchers as a bet that Theresa May will win a larger majority in the upcoming election, allowing her to pursue a softer Brexit and giving her more time to negotiate.

Pavlina Pizova, a Czech hiker, was found alive and in reasonable health after being missing for nearly a month in New Zealand's Fiordland National Park, where her hiking partner, Ondrej Petr, died in a hiking accident, and she then spent a month in a nearby hut before being rescued.

Millions of Russians, including Elena and her husband, are struggling with overwhelming debt, with over 40 million Russians having loans or mortgages, and at least 10% of the total personal debt of 1 trillion roubles (£10.7bn; $16.7bn) being unrecoverable by banks, with the average personal loan in 2014 being 54,600 roubles.
James Holmes, 24, is accused of killing 12 and wounding 58 people at a midnight showing of the new Batman movie in Colorado.

Art specialist Christopher Marinello, CEO of the Art Recovery Group, stresses that stopping the theft of Syria's precious antiquities necessitates a multi-faceted approach, primarily involving halting the war and educating collectors, dealers, and auction houses to eschew material lacking provenance.

The Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission's report on the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster found that it was a "manmade" disaster, resulting from a combination of collusion, lack of governance, and ingrained cultural conventions in Japan, including a reflexive obedience to authority, reluctance to question authority, and a groupistic mindset, which led to organisational and regulatory system failures.

The UK government's auto-enrolment programme has achieved a 95% compliance rate among small businesses, with 66% of employees now signed up, but concerns persist about the adequacy of employer contributions and the need for increased savings to ensure a decent retirement for millions of workers.

A Canadian-led team has calculated that the Earth's land surface contains a layer of water approximately 180m deep, with only 6% of it being "modern" groundwater that is extractable, sensitive to climate change and human contamination, and can be renewed on a human lifetime scale.

Edinburgh in Scotland has been chosen to host the 2017 European Rugby Challenge Cup finals, with the Challenge Cup and Champions Cup finals scheduled to take place on the same weekend, but with the Challenge Cup finals being held in Edinburgh and the Champions Cup finals in Lyon, France.

Edward Snowden, the former CIA worker who leaked details of US surveillance programmes, will remain in the transit zone at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport after his lawyer, Anatoly Kucherena, stated that Snowden's application for temporary asylum in Russia had not been processed.

Brazil's Attorney-General, Rodrigo Janot, has asked the Supreme Court to investigate former President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's alleged involvement in a multi-billion dollar kickback scheme at state-oil company Petrobras, with accusations including obstruction of justice, receiving illicit benefits, and potentially being a beneficiary of the scheme.

The UK government has rejected a recommendation to remove the Ministry of Defence's immunity from prosecution, despite a coroner's ruling that neglect contributed to the deaths of three SAS selection exercise participants in 2013, and the Health and Safety Executive issuing a censure over the MoD's failings, which the coroner and bereaved families believe would have led to greater accountability and safety improvements.

Leicester City, the defending Premier League champions, are struggling this season, having been beaten by League One side Millwall in the FA Cup, with their manager Claudio Ranieri (not Claude) urging his players to show more fight and determination.

HMRC is investigating dozens of footballers, agents, and clubs over potential irregularities in their tax affairs, particularly regarding image rights payments, with officials bringing in £158 million in tax yield over the last two years, and seven criminal investigations are also underway.

A treason investigation into two German journalists who published classified documents on online surveillance was launched, but ultimately suspended, sparking a national debate about freedom of the press and government influence over the courts, leading to the dismissal of the chief prosecutor.

UK Chancellor George Osborne's 2015 Budget speech largely ignored the South East region, focusing instead on measures to boost growth in the North and other parts of the country, in a move seen as a calculated risk to shore up support in marginal seats ahead of the general election, although it did include some targeted initiatives for the region.

Doncaster Rovers secured a 1-0 win over Colchester United, with Tommy Rowe scoring in the first half, despite Colchester creating several scoring opportunities and pressing hard throughout the match, but actually it was Rowe scoring in the last seconds of the first half.

Ross McEwan, the CEO of Royal Bank of Scotland, stated that the uncertainty caused by the potential UK EU referendum could slow down banking and predicted that interest rates would remain low for a long period, ideally beyond 2017.

Labour leader Ed Miliband stated that a Labour government would not form a deal with the SNP if it meant compromising on key issues, while SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon claimed that Labour would rather see the Conservatives back in power than work with the SNP, with polls suggesting a hung parliament could lead to a Conservative or Labour-SNP government.

University students Elliot Vale and Tia Mountain have designed an app called GeoRescue, which would provide information on natural disasters and guide people to safety using GPS and advanced map services, with the goal of saving lives in emergency situations.

Sir Timothy O'Shea, a university leader, has expressed concerns that proposed amendments to the Scottish government's Higher Education Governance Bill could be "inconsistent, incoherent and potentially very damaging" to his institution, particularly regarding the roles of the rector and senior lay member, citing a lack of consultation and potential unintended consequences.

Elena Hrabovenska, a Ukrainian-born owner of three Polish delis in the UK, expresses concern over the potential impact of the country's decision to leave the EU on her business and hopes that her community will not be driven apart by hate and intolerance, amid rising anti-migrant sentiment in her hometown of Peterborough.

Following the killing of five police officers in Dallas by Micah Johnson, the city's police department received an anonymous threat and took precautionary measures, including deploying SWAT officers and an armoured vehicle, but the city's main building remained open to the public despite heightened security.

Australian politicians, including Prime Minister Tony Abbott and opposition leader Bill Shorten, have expressed varying levels of commitment to accepting more Syrian and Iraqi refugees, with some calling for increased numbers and others proposing solutions, such as temporary housing.

UKIP leader Nigel Farage unveiled a campaign poster attacking the Conservatives' record on immigration, claiming that Britain's EU membership made it impossible to control immigration, and setting a target of reducing net migration to about 30,000 people per year.

Gareth Southgate has been appointed as the permanent manager of the England national team, signing a contract reportedly worth up to £2m a year, after a successful stint as interim boss, including a 3-0 win against Scotland in World Cup qualifying.

The FBI has ordered Apple to disable the security software on a dead murderer's iPhone, but Apple has refused, with CEO Tim Cook and Facebook's Mark Zuckerberg expressing concerns that complying would set a "dangerous" precedent for government access to encrypted data, while a lawyer representing some of the victims and others like Google and Twitter have backed the federal bureau.

Prince William praised his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, as a "guiding example" of a good monarch in a BBC interview, ahead of her 90th birthday, and discussed his own approach to royal duty and his future plans.

The new Star Trek film, Star Trek Beyond, has been defended by its cast and crew as a thoughtful and respectful representation of the character Sulu's diversity, despite criticism from George Takei, the original Sulu, who claimed it was a twisting of Gene Roddenberry's creation.

Peterborough United secured a 4-1 win over Bristol Rovers, with Jack Marriott scoring a hat-trick, including a goal in added time, after Posh took an early lead and maintained their advantage throughout the match.

Jihadist group IS launched an assault on the city of Tadmur, adjacent to the ancient Unesco World Heritage site of Palmyra, but its push was reportedly halted by the Syrian army, with warnings that IS would destroy the site if it falls under its control, and IS had already killed civilians and taken control of nearby areas.

Passengers on a high-speed train from Amsterdam to Paris described being abandoned by staff after a gunman opened fire, with staff members locking themselves away in a service area, leaving passengers to fend for themselves until heroic passengers intervened to overpower the attacker.

The British Olympic Association (BOA) has ratified the nomination of Lutalo Muhammad, ranked 59th in the world, over the world number one, Aaron Cook, for the 2012 London Olympics, citing that GB Taekwondo followed proper selection procedures, but expressing disappointment and concern over the lack of transparency in the decision.

Two British tourists, Hannah Witheridge and David Miller, were found dead on a beach in Thailand, with police initially investigating British brothers Christopher and James Ware and 11 Burmese people, but now having no DNA matches and admitting they "really don't know where to look now" after forensic tests revealed traces of semen from two different men that did not match anyone in their initial list of suspects.

Japan is preparing to host the 2019 Rugby World Cup, with the Olympic Games in Tokyo the following year expected to boost the country's sports enthusiasts' interest and provide a prime opportunity for rugby to gain popularity.

The success or failure of a revolution in a country depends on the interplay between the demand for change and the "supply-side" of revolution, particularly the army's ability and willingness to use force, with independent, professional armies often opting for a peaceful transition.

The UK's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in the three months to November, its lowest rate since October 2005, with the employment rate reaching 74.5%, a record high since comparable records began in 1971.
Middlesbrough secured their first home win of the season with a 2-0 victory over Bournemouth, thanks to goals from Gastón Ramírez and Stewart Downing.

The first practice session for the Chinese Grand Prix was disrupted by two left-rear wheel failures for Williams driver Felipe Massa and a suspected broken left rear suspension for Renault's Kevin Magnussen, leading to a 30-minute investigation and a shortened practice session, with the issue later found to be "rim clearance" for Massa's car.

Hibernian dominated Bonnyrigg Rose, scoring eight goals to their opponent's one, with Andrew Shinnie, James Keatings, Chris Humphrey, Jason Cummings (twice), Lewis Stevenson, Keatings again, and Jordan Forster scoring in a one-sided match.

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has expressed concerns about a proposed anti-homosexuality bill, stating he believes gay people are "abnormal" but does not support their persecution, despite the bill's provisions for life imprisonment and other severe penalties.

Cardiff manager Steve Slade, who has managed over 750 games, is confident that his team can reach the top six and the Premier League, despite having previously taken three teams to play-off finals without winning promotion.

Scotland women's national team captain, Jennifer Evans, is determined to secure a spot in the 2024 European Women's Football Championship finals after narrowly missing out in previous play-offs, and a win against Iceland on Friday would give them a strong chance of qualifying directly as one of the top six group runners-up.

Claire, a former event-rider paralyzed from the chest down after a 2006 horse riding accident, is training to walk 26 miles in the London marathon using a robotic walking suit, aiming to raise over £50,000 for Spinal Research and prove that with determination and resilience, anything is possible, despite initially being able to only take two steps and facing numerous challenges in her recovery.

Jack Walsh, a 23-year-old film enthusiast from Northern Ireland, is working behind the camera for the popular YouTube channel Game Grumps in Los Angeles, where he shoots and directs commercials, and is involved in the company's expansion into TV comedy on YouTube's Red channel, and also aspires to write and direct a Game Grumps musical.

Scotland's First Minister Nicola Sturgeon has been ranked 50th in Forbes magazine's annual list of the world's most powerful and influential women, alongside other notable figures including German Chancellor Angela Merkel, who topped the list for the sixth year in a row, Hillary Clinton, and Janet Yellen.

Researchers have found that many mammals, including reindeer, are sensitive to ultra-violet light emitted by power lines, which may be disrupting habitats and migration patterns by causing animals to avoid the lines, a phenomenon that could have a global impact on wildlife.

Former clients and employees of Kids Company, a UK-based charity, have made allegations of widespread sexual exploitation and abuse by clients, including forced sex and harassment, but it appears that some of these concerns were not reported to authorities despite staff being aware of them.

A year after the Brexit referendum, a Leave voter from North Yorkshire, Paul Austin, has expressed uncertainty about his decision, citing concerns over immigration, taxation, and quality control post-Brexit, as well as recent news events such as the Charlie Gard case and the Grenfell Tower fire, which have influenced his views on the UK's relationship with the EU.

England's tour of Pakistan ended in a draw, with debutant Adil Rashid taking five wickets to help his team come within 25 runs of a famous victory, but ultimately falling short due to the match being abandoned due to fading light.

Celtic manager Brendan Rodgers praised the performances of new signings Ollie Ntcham and Kundai Benyu, stating that they have the potential to be top-level players and expressing his enthusiasm for their contributions to the team, particularly Ntcham who was playing his first game after signing from Manchester City.

A shipment of 300 initial doses of a potentially preventative Ebola vaccine, produced by GlaxoSmithKline and the US National Institutes of Health, is expected to arrive in Monrovia, Liberia, one of the hardest hit countries, but experts warn that it may be challenging to establish the vaccine's effectiveness due to the declining number of Ebola cases.
Both teams had several scoring opportunities, but were unable to find the back of the net throughout the 90 minutes.

The Australian government has agreed to a last-minute settlement of A$70m with 1,905 asylum seekers who alleged they suffered harm while being held on Manus Island between 2012 and 2016, with the government citing the settlement as a "prudent" decision to avoid costly legal fees.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes, 37, has come out of retirement to help the team through their injury crisis, making a surprise appearance off the bench in a 3-2 win over Manchester City, after announcing his return just an hour before kick-off.

Mike Young, a 70-year-old animation producer from Wales, has spent his career creating beloved TV series such as SuperTed, which originated as bedtime stories for his stepson and went on to become a global phenomenon, and is now working on a feature-length animation and a new film project about a legendary Cardiff City football player, having previously lived in California and worked for major studios.

A surge in far-right and nationalist movements across Europe, driven by concerns over immigration and globalization, is reshaping the continent's political landscape, with parties like the Freedom Party in Austria, the Alternative for Germany, and the National Front in France, along with other nationalist parties such as the Sweden Democrats, the Swiss People's Party, and the Danish People's Party, gaining significant support.

Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy defended the club's lack of summer signings, while Chelsea manager Antonio Conte expressed admiration for Tottenham striker Harry Kane, who Conte believes would cost at least £100m if signed.
A total of 387 people were arrested between February 2016 and February 2017, up from 255 the previous year, prompting calls for tougher rules on alcohol sales at airports.

The British Racing Drivers' Club (BRDC), which owns the Silverstone circuit, will exercise a break clause in its contract after 2019, but both the BRDC and Formula 1's owner Liberty Media are open to continuing the British Grand Prix at Silverstone beyond that date.
Marcus Rashford scored the winning goal in the 90th minute, securing a 1-0 victory for Manchester United over Hull City, but the team's 100% record was actually from two games, not three.

Ben Stokes, the vice-captain of the England Test team, has stated that he still has a desire to be aggressive on the field, despite growing as a cricketer and receiving demerit points, and is looking to lead England to a win in their upcoming series against West Indies, who have a talented team capable of hitting the ball out of the ground.

In an effort to improve student outcomes, Coventry City College has implemented a radical approach to teaching English and maths GCSEs to students who did not achieve C grades at school, with the goal of helping them gain the essential skills needed to progress to vocational courses, apprenticeships, and successful careers, by providing one-on-one support and tailoring teaching to individual students' needs.

Welsh Transport Minister Ken Skates has accused Network Rail of a lack of investment in clearing leaves from rail lines, citing a 28-year timeline to bring the Welsh network up to standard, and has met with Network Rail officials to discuss the issue, after Arriva Trains Wales reported a significant increase in train removals due to damaged wheels.

The UK Government Minister for Wales, Simon Hart (not Simon Cairns), testified before the Welsh Affairs Select Committee, highlighting potential advantages of Brexit for Wales, including new international trade opportunities, while also addressing devolution, steel industry concerns, and the Severn crossings.
The Durham Jets secured their first win of the season, chasing down Leicestershire's 88-2 to win by 4 wickets, thanks to Paul Coughlin's 38 not out and Paul Collingwood's 34.

China, which has a rich history of innovation, is now undergoing a second industrial revolution, with a rapidly growing economy, ambitious space exploration plans, and a significant influence on the global market, despite facing challenges such as social discontent, corruption, and human rights concerns, and has become the world's second-largest economy since 2011.

Bookmakers William Hill, Ladbrokes, Coral, and Paddy Power have suspended betting on the James Bond theme song for Spectre after Radiohead emerged as a new favourite, with Ellie Goulding initially being a popular choice, following a cryptic hint from Goulding and confirmation from director Sam Mendes that a song has been recorded.

Nicola Sturgeon, the First Minister of Scotland, has ruled out an independence referendum in 2017, but has indicated that a vote could be held in the near future if the UK's Brexit negotiations do not favor Scotland's interests, potentially as early as the autumn of the following year.

Four men arrested on European arrest warrants as part of a coordinated operation involving six countries, appeared in court and refused extradition, with their lawyers potentially challenging the move due to the risk of refoulement, as they are suspected of being part of the Rawti Shax "jihadist network" seeking to establish a caliphate in Iraq's Kurdistan region, allegedly planning to free their leader, Mullah Krekar, who is in detention in Norway.

The UK's finances still have a long way to go, according to the Institute for Fiscal Studies' (IFS) Green Budget, which estimates that the country needs significant spending cuts, totaling £51.4 billion, or 14.1%, in the next parliament, with 98% of the remaining consolidation planned to come from spending cuts rather than higher taxes.
Cambridge United secured a 3-1 victory over Cheltenham Town, with Uche Ikpeazu and Luke Berry scoring two goals each, but Ikpeazu scored only one goal.

Police in Northern Ireland are investigating complaints about "distasteful" materials, including stolen election posters, Irish national flags, and racist messages, being placed on bonfires lit in loyalist areas to mark the Eleventh Night of July.

Broadcasters are developing companion apps that synchronize with TV shows, allowing viewers to engage with content and track conversations on social media, as they aim to harness the trend of using second-screen devices while watching TV.

Tech giants like Facebook and Google face pressure to remove far-right material online, but imposing stricter regulations risks undermining encryption and private companies' role in censoring content.

The Longford Town Centre, once a symbol of Ireland's economic downturn, is now showing signs of recovery, with local businesses reporting increased sales and a new Center Parcs development planned to bring in 1,000 jobs, but traders still feel that more needs to be done to boost local business, particularly in addressing issues like parking charges.

Swiss pilot André Borschberg has embarked on the seventh leg of his solo, around-the-world journey in the Solar Impulse aircraft, aiming to reach Hawaii after a 5-6 day continuous flight from China's Nanjing.

Former Archbishop of Canterbury Lord Carey has dropped his opposition to the Assisted Dying Bill, stating that he has changed his mind due to the reality of "needless suffering" and believes it is not "anti-Christian" to support the change in the law, while current Archbishop Justin Welby remains opposed, citing concerns that it would put pressure on vulnerable people to end their lives, specifically mentioning the elderly and disabled individuals.

The international community has condemned North Korea's reported H-bomb test, prompting various proposed solutions on social media, including increased UN action, dialogue with North Korea, imposing sanctions, and seeking the help of a mediator.

Refugees and asylum seekers living in Belfast, including those from Algeria, Sudan, and Colombia, are participating in a volunteer conservation program with the Mourne Heritage Trust, where they work together to rebuild dry-stone walls and repair mountain paths in the Mourne mountains of County Down, finding peace and a sense of belonging in their new home.

England's Stuart Broad took 5-1 in 31 balls to lead his team to a remarkable victory, while the article highlights the team's ability to turn matches around with multiple match-winners, including Broad, Ben Stokes, and Joe Root, who are well-positioned for future series against Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and Australia.

Scientists have created the most detailed continent-wide map of groundwater reserves in Africa, revealing that the total volume of water in aquifers underground is 100 times the amount found on the surface, and that many countries considered "water scarce" have substantial hidden water reserves, but caution that large-scale drilling may not be the best way to access these resources.

Former UK cabinet secretary Lord O'Donnell predicts that the UK's separation from the EU will take "years and years and years," citing the EU's reluctance to make radical changes, the complexity of the Brexit process, and the difficulty of implementing the people's decision.

A 22-year-old woman, Sian O'Callaghan, has gone missing after leaving a nightclub in Marlborough, with over 60 police officers working on the investigation and hundreds of volunteers joining the search in Savernake Forest, following her phone being tracked to the area 32 minutes after she left the club.

Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen set the fastest lap time in the second Chinese Grand Prix practice session, with a 0.109-second lead over his teammate, ahead of a potential threat to Mercedes' dominance, as Ferrari hinted they may challenge Mercedes this weekend.

A group of people affected by the Thalidomide drug scandal, including former mayor Kim Fenton, are campaigning for the German government to recognize its responsibilities and provide proper compensation to survivors, with an EU resolution expected to be passed in January that could pressure the country to take action.

Eli Wallach, a character actor known for his versatility and wide range of roles, received an honorary Oscar in 2011 for his contributions to film, spanning six decades and including iconic roles in The Magnificent Seven, The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, and The Godfather: Part II.

Hanson Academy sent almost 10% of its pupils home on Tuesday for failing to meet the school's strict uniform policy, with parents expressing frustration and financial concerns about the new measures, despite the school claiming it had communicated its expectations clearly.
Clashes broke out in Beirut between Sunni groups, with some pro-Syrian and others anti-Syrian, following the shooting deaths of two anti-Syrian clerics.

Nick Clegg argued that a stable and strong coalition involving his Liberal Democrats was necessary to save the country from a potential re-run election, warning that minority governments formed by Labour and the Conservatives would be unstable and lead to controversy, rather than a coalition led by his party.

Liverpool suffered a second-half collapse in the Champions League final, losing to Sevilla and missing out on European football next season, with manager Jürgen Klopp promising to use the setback as an opportunity to improve the team.

A 25-year-old man has been killed in a violent incident in Sparkbrook, Birmingham, where a 25-year-old is in critical condition with knife wounds and a 22-year-old is being treated for non-life-threatening gunshot injuries.

South Africa's Competition Commission has launched a two-year investigation into 17 major banks, including Barclays, JP Morgan, and HSBC, for allegedly colluding to manipulate currency markets through online chat rooms, with the banks facing potential fines and prosecution, dating back as far as 2007.

Jonathan Bell, a DUP MLA, alleged that two DUP special advisers, Peter Robinson and Timothy Johnston, had attempted to influence the Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) scheme, but both men denied these claims and said they had no personal or family financial interests in the scheme, with Robinson later revealing a family connection to the poultry industry.

Scientists have developed a technique called GESTALT, which uses CRISPR gene editing to insert a "molecular barcode" into the genome, allowing researchers to record and trace the lineage of individual cells in an organism, potentially leading to profound insights into normal, diseased, or damaged tissues.

A business owner, who invested £100,000 in a boiler and received £5,200 in annual payment under the capped Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) scheme, had his attempt to block the publication of his details by the Department for the Economy partially rejected by a court, with the department arguing that including the date of application would allow the public to differentiate between capped and uncapped payments.

South African judge Thokozile Masipa sentenced Oscar Pistorius, the Olympic and Paralympic athlete, to five years in prison for culpable homicide in the death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, with the possibility of serving only 10 months and the remainder under house arrest, or possibly two years.

Tunisia is grappling with the aftermath of its worst-ever terror attack, which has left a nation in shock, threatened the country's tourism industry, and prompted the government to implement a security clampdown.

British Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond's visit to Tripoli aims to provide international backing and £10m-worth of aid to the fledgling Government of National Accord, amidst growing concerns over Islamic State's presence and the refugee crisis, with potential military assistance and a possible European force deployment being considered.

The Beyond Caravaggio exhibition at the National Galleries in Scotland features the work of Italian artist Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio and 30 other artists from Europe who were influenced by him, showcasing a collection of paintings that explore Caravaggio's revolutionary art and its impact on the art world, including the painting "The Taking of Christ" which was initially offered to the Scottish National Gallery for free in 1921 but was turned down.

Two men, Virgilio Correia and Christopher Menaul, have been sentenced to at least 16 and 9 years in prison respectively for the murder of Wing Fu Cheung, who was stabbed 18 times during a robbery in January 2015, with the judge describing the attackers as "drug-addled, parasitic assailants" motivated by a desire to pay off a drugs debt, and also received additional sentences for wounding and robbery.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has introduced a new county cricket schedule, aiming to make the sport more attractive to future generations by reducing the number of games, improving the structure, and promoting the T20 Blast during school summer holidays, while also increasing the profile of the One-Day Cup and potentially making the T20 Blast more widely available on television.

The US economy posted annualized growth of 2.6% in the fourth quarter, driven by a 4.3% rise in consumer spending, but the pace of growth was lower than expected and some economists are concerned that it may be too reliant on consumer spending, which was partly offset by a 1.9% annualized decline in business investment.

The devolution of corporation tax to Northern Ireland is being delayed due to the failure of the Welfare Reform Bill to pass at Stormont, which has led to uncertainty over the future of the tax and caused companies to defer investment decisions, despite the legislation to allow Corporation Tax powers to be devolved to Stormont having been passed by the House of Lords in March.

Musician Chris Rea shares his lifelong passion for Formula 1, recalling his childhood fascination with iconic drivers like Wolfgang Alexander von Trips and later experiencing the sport firsthand as a mechanic for Eddie Irvine's team, while also lamenting the current state of the sport, which he believes has lost its raw, mechanical appeal.

Margaret Thatcher, the UK's first female prime minister, died at 87 in 2013, leaving behind a legacy of significant changes to Britain, including privatization, reduced government control, and economic growth, but also sparking controversy and protests during her 11-year rule, which ended in 1990.

Ian Brady, a 75-year-old serial killer, has been ruled by a mental health tribunal to continue receiving medical treatment at Ashworth Hospital due to his chronic mental illness and paranoid schizophrenia.

Musa Bility, the president of the Liberian Football Association, has threatened to take Fifa's Ad-Hoc Electoral Committee to the Court of Arbitration for Sport if committee head Domenico Scala does not withdraw from the presidential election due to a potential conflict of interest, citing Scala's shared nationality with Gianni Infantino, one of the five candidates.

Brock Turner, a 21-year-old former Stanford University swimmer, was released from jail after serving three months for assaulting an unconscious woman, despite prosecutors' demands for a six-year sentence, sparking widespread criticism and calls for reform in California's sex assault laws, including the amendment of a loophole that allowed for more lenient sentences in cases where no force was used.

Stephen Beadman, 29, has admitted raping and murdering 15-year-old Kayleigh Haywood, and Luke Harlow, 27, is on trial for false imprisonment, having previously pleaded guilty to sexual grooming and other charges related to his abuse of the teenager, with the false imprisonment charge specifically alleged to have occurred after Kayleigh had already been raped and murdered.

The UK's referendum on European Union membership resulted in a narrow majority voting to leave the EU, driven by a north-south divide, with the north of England voting to leave and Scotland voting to remain, leading to potential implications for the country's future.

Thousands of rail workers, including signallers and maintenance staff, are set to strike for 24 hours on Monday, potentially causing widespread cancellations and disruptions to services on various train lines, including Scotrail, Virgin West Coast, and Southeastern, as well as other operators such as CrossCountry Trains, Chiltern Railways, and First Great Western.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) is planning to condense the Six Nations tournament from seven weeks to six, but several players and officials, including Wales' Gareth Davies and Scotland's Mark Dodson, have expressed concerns over the potential impact on player safety and the integrity of the game, with a specific focus on the proposed changes and the independent review of Wales' controversial match against France.

Johann Lamont, the Scottish Labour leader, has resigned, accusing the UK Labour party leadership of treating Scotland like a "branch office" and criticizing those who undermined her position as she sought to reform the party in Scotland, with several senior Labour figures expressing anger and concern over her departure.

This weekend in European football saw several teams crowned champions, including Club Brugge in Belgium, Benfica in Portugal, and Besiktas in Turkey, while other teams like Stuttgart in Germany and Carpi in Italy faced relegation.

The UK Department for Education overspent £1 billion on its academy expansion programme between 2010 and 2012, with total expenditure reaching £8.3 billion, largely due to the rapid and unanticipated growth in the number of schools converting to academy status, which required the department to find additional funding from other budgets to remain within overall spending limits.

Campaigners are warning that a government requirement for nursery workers to have a grade C in GCSE English and maths is blocking staff career paths, deterring new starters, and potentially leading to a recruitment crisis that could jeopardize the quality of childcare and government plans for 30 hours of free childcare, citing a 30% drop in students completing the Level 3 Early Years Educator course.

During his presidential campaign, Donald Trump expressed numerous controversial and often contradictory views on various issues, including national security, immigration, climate change, healthcare, and more, which he often modified, reversed, or clarified.
Business leaders and rock music legends share advice on building successful businesses, emphasizing the importance of passion, innovation, and adaptability in a rapidly changing market.
